result.content:
# Proposed discovery plan

Determine whether to develop and launch a dedicated handoff tracker tailored for small software development teams in Latvia.

## Proposed scope

- Workflow and status handoff tracking for small software teams based in Latvia.
- Assessment of current manual handoff practices and friction points.
- Excludes any payroll, accounting, or financial advisory functionality.

Region: Latvia

Explicit exclusions: Do not include payroll or financial advice

## Engineering Team Lead

Responsible for coordinating team deliverables, weekly transitions, and operational documentation.

- How many hours per week does your team spend preparing and sharing handoff updates? (question-f33e340c52a99112794296da)
- What challenges do existing issue trackers present when transferring task context between team members? (question-0a140c228353a6233090a5ee)

## Engineering Manager

Evaluates developer productivity, workflow tooling, and software budget allocation for development teams.

- What criteria would justify investing in a dedicated handoff tracking solution over existing general-purpose software? (question-61518d078c781defc9288b5c)

## Simulation hypotheses

- We spend two hours copying handoff updates each Friday. [source:operator-interview]

## Assumptions

- Small software development teams in Latvia face recurring friction when transferring task context at the end of the work week.
- Teams currently rely on manual copy-paste routines to synchronize project state across multiple channels.

## Evidence gaps

- No verified market research on the size, tool stack, or budget constraints of software teams in Latvia.
- Lack of customer interviews confirming whether Friday handoff overhead leads to delivery delays or lost work.
- No non-synthetic source findings were established; the plan is a proposal, not customer validation.

This scope is proposed, not a claim of user approval.

## Selected sources

- [source:operator-interview] Synthetic operator interview fixture — synthetic_transcript
